QF.id: AIFM CII AIFs in India and Suitability_9

question.text: Mr. Deepak Verma (HNI) has decided to deploy INR 20 crore across a Category II AIF allocation that mirrors the Illustration-2 template in Chapter 3 — i.e., 25% to Emerging Technologies/IT-focussed AIFs, 35% to Non-IT/Sector-agnostic AIFs, 10% Pre-IPO Placements, 10% PIPEs/Listed Stock, 10% M&A/Co-investment, and 10% Private Credit / Special Situation Debt Funds. What is the COMBINED rupee allocation to 'Emerging-Tech/IT-focussed AIFs' PLUS 'Private Credit / Special Situation Debt Funds'?

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Emerging Tech/IT = 25% of INR 20 crore = INR 5 crore. Private Credit / SSF = 10% of INR 20 crore = INR 2 crore. Combined = INR 5 crore + INR 2 crore = INR 7 crore. This mirrors Illustration 2 in Section 3.4.2 where the investor keeps 75% in later-stage unlisted space (Series C) and 25% in Pre-IPO/market opportunities/special situations. **The Trap:** INR 5 crore ignores the SSF bucket. INR 9 crore adds Non-IT (which was not asked). INR 12 crore adds Emerging Tech + Non-IT (25%+35%), which is 60% and ignores the actual question. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-A and XIX-C test allocation tables with the same illustrations. XXI-B tests PMS allocation math. In all cases, watch the percentage-to-rupee arithmetic carefully — examiners often hide the trick in the question wording ('combined', 'excluding', 'net of fees'). **Manager's Pro-Tip:** When presenting this diversification to an HNI, always layer a second dimension — vintage — on top of the sector cut. A 25% tech allocation deployed in one vintage year is NOT the same as 25% staggered over three vintages. Vintage diversification is the silent risk management lever Cat II managers understate.
